page: OVHcloud b3-8 is a general-purpose virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, delivering 2 vCPUs. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core performance ranking in the top 25 percent. However, multi-core scaling is more limited, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling into the average and weak categories respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance for large-block reads and writes, but weak performance for small-block cached reads.

The server exhibits lower performance in highly parallelized or memory-intensive tasks, as evidenced by weak scores in software compilation, database operations, and Redis SET operations. Static web serving throughput is also low, placing in the bottom 10 percent. Consequently, this instance is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic text processing, single-threaded applications, or development environments rather than high-throughput web serving or complex database hosting.
description: The OVHcloud b3-8 is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores running at 2.3 GHz, paired with 8.0 GB of RAM and 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmarks reveal strong single-core CPU performance, though multi-core scaling and memory bandwidth are more modest, placing in the average to weak categories. The server shows lower throughput in database operations and static web serving, making it less suitable for high-traffic applications. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for entry-level dedicated resource needs, making it a practical fit for lightweight general-purpose workloads, single-threaded tasks, development environments, and basic text processing.
